title: Learning to arrange with Charlie Johnson
summary: Carter began arranging sax choruses for three Bennys, studied stock arrangements and taught himself scoring the hard way.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Right. Okay. Now, let's go on to the subject of arranging.
Now when did the arranging come in, and let's bring that up to 1928, sort of, or up to the point where you joined Fletcher Henderson.

Actually, I started arranging when I was with Charlie Johnson's orchestra at the Small's Paradise. I started arranging by writing saxophone choruses, you know, for 3 saxophones, because that's what we had then, and there were 3 saxophones -- Benny Whittet, Benny Waters and Benny Carter. Three Bennys in the saxophone section.

And I used to write the saxophone choruses, you know, the rhythm section, because they knew all the chord changes and I knew the chord changes, but I didn't know how to do anything else. And I decided I wanted to arrange. I started studying what they called 'stock arrangements' -- arrangements by Don Redman, Archie Blyer, Arthur Lang, Walter Paul; I guess, Jimmy Dale, Jack Mason ... these are the names I remember, and I used to layout the parts on the floor and study them. And I started arranging just like that; part by part -- starting with the first trumpet, second trumpet, etc., and was oh, I guess, quite -- it was quite a matter of months before I knew how to make a score, you know? Because
I was doing it the hard way.
Yeah. Let me go back for a moment. You started the actual arranging, and your arrangements were used when you were with Charlie Johnson, let's say, 1927?
But had you been interested in arranging? Did you have some ambition to arrange? Had you made some attempts on your own which were not arrangements that perhaps were not actually used?
Well, I don't remember that I did. I don't think I did anything for the Henderson band, you know, Horace Henderson, that is.
Did Charlie Johnson ask you to do some arrangements, or did you ...

No, I just started bringing these things and I would ask other saxophone players to join me and try them, you know ... like if we'd play a song like "I Got Rhythm" or one of the, you know, we'd use the saxophone chorus in the arrangement or something. Even if it was somebody else's arrangement or something.
I see. And the musicians liked them, or at least the musicians liked them.
Yes, they seemed to like them.
And when you say you learned the hard way, you didn't have a teacher, also? Nobody said to
No, I didn't have enough sense to do that. That was too easy.
